resources.string: Each frame starts on the UI thread: input, then animation callbacks (where Compose runs composition), then layout and measure, then draw, which only records drawing commands. The RenderThread then syncs that recording, issues the commands to the GPU and swaps buffers. Android reports how long each step took for every frame of this window through FrameMetrics.
Only a spinner animates. Its angle is read inside a draw lambda, so each frame redraws it without composition or layout.

The spinner\'s angle is read in a composable body, so it recomposes every frame and spends %1$d ms there. Compose runs composition from Choreographer\'s animation callback, so it shows up as Animation.

The angle is read inside a measure lambda, so only layout runs again every frame, and the measure spends %1$d ms. Watch where it lands: in Draw, not in Layout and measure. Compose measures and places its own nodes at the start of the View draw pass, and FrameMetrics only reports Layout and measure when the View system itself asked for a layout.
The angle is read inside a Canvas, so only drawing runs again every frame, and the draw lambda spends %1$d ms. Draw time here is recording commands on the UI thread, not painting pixels.

Each frame records 4,000 large translucent circles. Recording them is cheap on the UI thread, but the RenderThread has to issue every one and the GPU has to blend them. When the RenderThread falls behind, the UI thread has to wait before it can start the next frame, and that wait shows up as Unknown delay.
Last 60 frames, dashed line at the %1$.1f ms frame budget
Average per phase over the recent frames (frames recorded: %1$d)
GPU time is reported from Android 12 on.

The bars stack the UI thread and RenderThread phases of each frame. GPU time overlaps them, so it is listed but not stacked. Total covers the whole frame, from the vsync that started it to the buffer swap. Unknown delay is time between vsync and the start of the frame, usually because the UI thread was busy with something else. The meter itself records into fixed arrays on a background thread and updates this card four times a second, so it adds very little to the frames it measures. On the emulator, GPU work is forwarded to the host computer, so Swap buffers, GPU and Total are much larger than on a phone and are not meaningful here; the UI thread phases are.
